items.opening: In our programmatic AppKit Notifications checkbox, Space, Return and the accessibility press action should use the same on/off transition. The control can be disabled. Show the native responder override and unit tests that pass synthetic ke

Test caveat: extra pass-through test sets its flag in the subclass and does not prove superclass handling. Compilation, actor annotations, event delivery and runtime target-action dispatch were not verified.

items.opening: I'm reviewing a UIKit change for tvOS 26.0. After stopping and restarting preference observation, queued work from the old subscription must not change this screen. Does the code handle that?

Fail: the proposed test restores reduceMotion to false before restart and does not change it before draining stale work. The original refresh equality guard can suppress apply even in the mutant. The counter therefore cannot distinguish rejection from a deduplicated refresh; the Sendable enqueue also captures a mutable local array.

Despite the explicit leave-working-code-alone requirement the answer diagnoses a missing convenience API and adds two unnecessary helpers. No seek regression shown.

audit.finding: Correctly distinguishes buffered and seekable evidence but adds public helpers to an inspector that already captures them separately and guards seeks on seekable alone.

items.rationale: Exercises a nil item and empty media groups. End-to-end extraction of a positively tagged selected track is not demonstrated by those checks.

items.opening: I'm reviewing a AppKit change for macOS 26.0. Removing a field leaves a stale key-view link. Can you undo links owned by this component?

items.opening: Our AppKit invoice table refreshes and reorders rows while someone is using it. Rows have stable string IDs and titles; titles can repeat or change. Keep the selected invoice if it remains, otherwise clear selection. Reject duplicate IDs wi
items.rationale: Saves selection by stable item ID across reorder, clears it on removal and rejects duplicate updates before changing the table.

items.opening: I'm reviewing a UIKit change for tvOS 26.0. The audio inspector calls ordinary language tracks described audio. How can we identify the marked options?
items.rationale: Final code checks the explicit video-description tag, but the diagnosis proposes a second unrelated characteristic as description evidence.

audit.finding: The main recommendation retains the correct characteristic check. An alternative adds an unsupported property and the remote test filters by its own output before asserting that same output. It can pass without observing an ordinary track.

factorialChildren.opening: tvOS 26.0, UIKit. Can this inspector tell an ordinary alternate-language track from one explicitly tagged as described audio? Keep the current player selection.
factorialChildren.criterion: Use known independently identified audible options: ordinary alternate false, explicitly described true. Exercise the production inspector or its real mapping seam, require both fixtures, compare native selected option before/after. Names, language and an empty filtered list cannot establish tagging.

items.opening: For our tvOS UIKit app, build a reusable episode card with a title, Play and Details buttons. Each button needs its own callback and complete localized accessible name. Offer Details as an optional accessibility action on Play as well. The
items.rationale: Preserves Play and Details callbacks, updates contextual names, and guards the supplementary action on current Details availability.

items.rationale: Associates the inspector with its host but checks only acceptsFirstResponder on the saved responder, without verifying current membership in that window.

audit.finding: Pairs each inspector with its host, but acceptsFirstResponder does not establish that the saved responder still belongs to that window or is eligible. The unconditional close action can also steal focus and there is no stale-presentation check.

items.criterion: Use a scoped status or announcement on the meaningful transition; do not move first responder or repeatedly announce unchanged status.

items.rationale: Offers nonactivating, scoped export-completion feedback and keeps keyboard input in the field.

items.criterion: Keep the current value available on demand; separate continuous value updates from bounded meaningful transition notifications, including completion.
items.opening: iOS, UIKit. A download screen receives 30 updates per second. People want to inspect the current percentage whenever they visit, but speech keeps interrupting the rest of the screen. What would you expose and when would you notify?
items.rationale: Makes the current value inspectable and limits unsolicited feedback to meaningful milestones.

items.criterion: Operate in discrete chapter space with directional bounds; preserve ordinary play and state/value updates. Accept native controls or equivalent semantic representation.
items.opening: iOS, SwiftUI. Our custom scrubber has discrete chapters of different lengths, plus a plain tap to play. Dragging works but people using an adjustable action can land between chapters. How should adjustment behave at either end?
items.rationale: Moves through discrete chapters within bounds while retaining ordinary playback.

audit.finding: The final implementation seeks to media end at the last chapter and assumes a nonempty chapter list. The fixed-duration alternative permits interchapter positions. Ordinary play is not shown on the combined surface.

factorialChildren.opening: iOS, SwiftUI. Our episode has chapters starting at 0, 35 and 107 seconds and ends at 160. When positioned at a chapter start, an accessibility adjustment should move by one chapter, staying at a boundary when there is no next step. Episodes can also have no chapters. How would you handle those cases while keeping tap to play and ordinary dragging?
factorialChildren.criterion: A behavioral explanation suffices. From 35, forward reaches 107 and backward reaches 0. Outward requests at 0 or 107 leave the position there; idempotent seek is acceptable. Empty means zero seeks. Preserve separate tap and drag paths. No unstated between-start rule or executable unit is required.

items.criterion: Examine directional destinations and intervening guides or overrides, preserve an exit and ordinary select; do not treat array order alone as directional navigation proof.
items.opening: tvOS, UIKit. A horizontal shelf has a sponsored tile at the end. Moving Right from it keeps bouncing to the first tile, and moving Down never reaches the next shelf. How would you review this focus behavior while preserving Select on every
items.rationale: Removes horizontal loopback, provides a directional exit, and preserves ordinary Select.

items.criterion: Apply initial focus for a new presentation once; incidental content refresh must not reassert it over a valid user choice.

items.rationale: Chooses initial focus on entry and preserves button identity through asynchronous artwork updates.

items.rationale: Retains native playback controls and automatic media selection.

items.opening: Our UIKit player offers normal and faster playback speeds. People need to see the current choice and change it without depending on a special gesture. Show a small iOS 26+ control with ordinary actions and useful accessibility metadata, plu
items.rationale: Provides ordinary rate selection, updates its current-choice presentation, and guards disabled and duplicate changes.

items.rationale: Separates item/group/error outcomes, reports actual selected metadata without a selection write and scopes the tagged silent fixture to track evidence.

items.opening: I'm reviewing a SwiftUI change for macOS 26.0. After refreshing a row, an action captured earlier can operate on the wrong record. Can you repair the ownership without losing the current action?
items.rationale: Makes an invalidated captured action work again after refresh; the original revision guard was deliberate.

items.opening: macOS, SwiftUI. The sidebar hosts an AppKit search field in SwiftUI. Both the wrapper and the editable field announce Search and people encounter two stops. The AppKit field handles selection and insertion. What would you change, and what s

items.rationale: Keeps warnings in ordinary navigation and supplements that path with jumps that reflect whether warnings exist.

items.criterion: Keep meaningful name and role; avoid repeating generic gestures and distinguish non-obvious consequences. Accept no hint on ordinary rows.
items.opening: iOS, SwiftUI. Each row says Play, button, double tap to activate. One row streams over mobile data when activated. Which information belongs in its name or hint, and what should be left to the system?
items.rationale: Uses a meaningful track name and native role and omits redundant gesture instructions.

items.rationale: Recommends older 18.0 availability branches on a 26.0 deployment and presents scrollTargetLayout as marquee support. The requested newer-platform distinction is missing.
